journeys.title: Build regression triage over recorded facts and explicit caveats
journeys.primary_decision: Explain, mitigate, or escalate a rebuild or build-slowdown regression without relying on folklore.
journeys.trigger_moment: A workspace maintainer or build engineer sees a rebuild surprise, CI slowdown, or migration breakage and needs a same-day explanation.
major_steps: Capture one bounded build-state pack from local or CI context.
Diff the current pack against a recent known-good or warm-build reference.
Attach build-dir or adapter caveats instead of laundering them away.
Escalate only the concrete unexplained deltas into issue or migration follow-up.
proof_of_completion: A maintainer can point to concrete rebuild reasons, timing deltas, and remaining unknowns.
The team changes what it does next based on the receipt rather than on anecdote.
anti_goals: Do not become a universal build daemon or hidden cache empire.
Do not sell target-dir archaeology as stable contract truth.
journeys.credible_home: companion-first cargo-* review tool over bounded Cargo facts
notes: This is the clearest cross-seam journey because the substrate is moving and the operator pain is broad.
The journey should preserve unknowns introduced by nightly-only or internal-layout surfaces.

journeys.title: Dependency admission and publish review over route truth, waivers, and release posture
journeys.primary_decision: Admit, quarantine, waive, or recheck a publish or dependency-intake decision with explicit route posture.
journeys.trigger_moment: A maintainer is about to publish a crate or adopt a dependency and wants reviewable security, route, and waiver posture.
major_steps: Import local package facts and publish-route details.
Pull in service truth such as Trusted Publishing posture or registry signals.
Make any waiver or quarantine decision explicit and bounded.
Record the final admit, recheck, or block posture with reasons.
proof_of_completion: The publish or dependency decision includes visible route posture and waiver context.
A later reviewer can reconstruct why the decision was made.
anti_goals: Do not become a universal crate trust score.
Do not erase context behind waivers or blocked routes.
journeys.credible_home: companion review kit importing crates.io and Cargo truth
notes: The key missing thing is the review journey, not one universal registry verdict.
Capability analysis can join later, but it should not replace explicit route review.

journeys.title: Debug issue handoff with tuple identity and explicit degraded-state posture
journeys.primary_decision: Route, reproduce, or narrow a debugging problem with enough context that another person can act on it.
journeys.trigger_moment: A debugging problem needs to be compared across debugger, OS, runtime, and async conditions or handed off into issue/support context.
major_steps: Capture tuple identity and scenario descriptors.
Attach build-state or reproduction context when it materially affects the failure.
Export a session pack that preserves unsupported or degraded states.
Route the result into issue, support, or regression-tracking channels.
proof_of_completion: A downstream maintainer can tell what tuple failed and what still needs reproduction.
The report makes degraded or unsupported posture visible instead of pretending green support.
anti_goals: Do not begin as a debugger fork.
Do not hide tuple caveats behind IDE-only magic.
journeys.credible_home: commons corpus plus companion export tooling
notes: The journey ends in a better handoff, not in a universal debugger UX story.
Tuple coverage drift should feed watchcards and packet refreshes, not just issue volume.

journeys.title: Release-boundary review with claim packs, witness programs, and explicit waivers
journeys.primary_decision: Cut, block, or waive a release-boundary claim with explicit evidence and import caveats.
journeys.trigger_moment: A maintainer is preparing a release and needs a reviewable answer to what changed at the public boundary and what remains unknown.
major_steps: Collect boundary facts from rustdoc JSON and other declared machine-readable surfaces.
Run witness-oriented or compile-based compatibility checks where available.
Preserve format-version and cross-crate visibility caveats instead of hiding them.
Record accept, block, or waive posture as part of release review.
proof_of_completion: Reviewers can distinguish supported claims from lossy imports and waivers.
The release decision is more explicit than “probably semver-safe.”
anti_goals: Do not claim one universal public-API truth source.
Do not treat machine-readable imports as caveat-free.
journeys.credible_home: companion-first release tooling with narrow Cargo adjacency
notes: This journey is moving closer to real Cargo-adjacent practice, but it should stay explicit about witness and waiver posture.
Cross-crate visibility limits are a major reason this should remain caveat-heavy.

journeys.title: Safety readiness evaluation with gap cards, lifecycle notes, and renewal ownership
journeys.primary_decision: Say yes, not yet, or only with mitigations to Rust in a regulated or qualification-sensitive context.
journeys.trigger_moment: An organization needs to know what evidence, dependency posture, interop practice, and renewal ownership would be required before moving forward.
major_steps: Pick a bounded domain or subsystem rather than a generic safety claim.
Map required evidence and lifecycle posture for dependencies and toolchain surfaces.
Record interop and boundary-management caveats explicitly.
Name renewal or stewardship owners before calling the path credible.
proof_of_completion: Stakeholders can explain why the answer is yes, not yet, or only with mitigations.
The journey produces owner-bearing renewal posture instead of aura.
anti_goals: Do not collapse many domains into one fake safety badge.
notes: This journey is stewardship-heavy on purpose and should remain domain-bounded.
FFI and boundary management are part of the journey, not a side note.

journeys.title: Conservative default selection with renewal receipts and explicit stale posture
journeys.primary_decision: Choose one conservative starting stack or default without pretending it is the universal best answer.
journeys.trigger_moment: A newcomer, domain guide, or internal platform lead needs a bounded starting recommendation for a specific Rust use case.
major_steps: Constrain the question to one domain or deployment shape.
Reuse evidence-bearing defaults rather than recomputing from vibes.
Attach renewal, stale, or unsupported posture visibly.
Give reconsider triggers rather than pretending the default is timeless.
proof_of_completion: A user can adopt one conservative default with eyes open.
The recommendation carries freshness and caveat posture instead of portal sprawl.
anti_goals: Do not become a giant Rust portal or leaderboard.
Do not recommend without renewal and stale-state posture.
journeys.credible_home: small evidence-bearing atlas layer with explicit owners
notes: This stays narrow on purpose because recommendation burden is high and renewal is expensive.
The right first contribution is a conservative default with receipts, not a sprawling atlas.
